description: Offline regression from the 24-attempt bottle-holder run: only geometry and reviews.

environment.note: Desk top at z = 0, its edge face at x = 0

environment.name: bottle
environment.note: Stands in the cup just past the desk edge, dropped in from above

environment.name: clamp_nut

initial_spec.name: Desk Water Bottle Holder

clamp_spine_t.note: spine thickness past the desk edge

desk_thick.note: Desk top thickness, from the request

initial_spec.summary: Screw clamp on the desk edge; the bottle stands in a cup beside the desk, joined to the clamp's spine.

issues.evidence: cup_floor_t = 3 mm; deflection 0.048 mm and peak stress 0.57 MPa are well within limits, but the floor is the first load-bearing feature and sees the full 14.7 N point load.
issues.fix: Consider increasing cup_floor_t to 4–5 mm in a future revision for durability, or add a subtle rib pattern (not modelled here) if weight is a concern.
issues.problem: The cup floor is 3 mm thick and the bottle load is applied directly on its top face. While deflection and stress checks pass, a 3 mm floor under a 1.5 kg bottle is thin for repeated impact loads (setting the bottle down hard).

issues.evidence: clamp_jaw_t = 10.2 mm; screw hole radius 3 mm at x = -20 mm; lower jaw spans x = -40 to 6 mm, so wall thickness on either side of hole is ~2.1 mm.
issues.fix: If the screw is a thumb-screw that bears on the jaw face, the current geometry is acceptable. If a nut bears on the jaw, consider a counter-bore or thicker jaw locally.
issues.problem: The screw hole is a 6 mm diameter through-hole in the 10.2 mm thick lower jaw, leaving only ~2.1 mm wall on each side of the hole. This is printable (min_wall check passes at 3 mm) but offers little bearing area for the M6 screw threads or head.

issues.evidence: Web occupies x = 3–26 mm, y = -20–20 mm, z = -60 to -10 mm; it is the only connection between cup and clamp spine.
issues.fix: Add a stiffening rib or flange on the web (e.g., a 3 mm thick T-rib along its centre) in a later optimisation round if mass budget allows.
issues.problem: The web (3 mm to 26 mm in x, full 40 mm in y, 50 mm tall) carries the entire bottle moment into the clamp spine. It is a single flat plate; buckling out-of-plane is not checked by the current linear stress/deflection analysis.

issues.evidence: features:9 defines a subtract cylinder at z=-64.0 with length_mm=5.0 (bottom at -64.0, top at -59.0). features:3 shows the cup floor is a solid cylinder from z=-63.0 to -60.0 (thickness 3.0 mm). The hole stops 1 mm short of the floor's top surface, leaving a 1 mm resin trap and no drainage path.
issues.fix: Make the drain hole penetrate the full floor thickness (length_mm ≥ cup_floor_t + small clearance, e.g., 4 mm) so it opens to the cup interior, or remove it if a drain is not required.
issues.problem: The drain hole is a 4 mm radius (8 mm diameter) blind hole drilled 5 mm deep into the cup floor from below. It does not break through the 3 mm thick floor, so it traps liquid resin during printing and cannot drain the cup in use.

issues.evidence: features:6 defines the clamp screw hole as a subtract cylinder with radius_mm=3.0. The hardware spec (M6 screw) and resin printing best practice call for +0.2 to +0.4 mm clearance on the nominal 3.0 mm radius.
issues.fix: Increase the screw hole radius to 3.2–3.4 mm.
issues.problem: The M6 clearance hole is modeled at 3.0 mm radius (6.0 mm diameter). For reliable threading and screw passage in Alpha Fast Resin, a 3.2–3.4 mm radius (6.4–6.8 mm diameter) is recommended to account for resin shrinkage and support residue.

issues.evidence: features:4 shows a 50 mm tall cylinder with 3 mm wall thickness. The design_intent assumes 'Print orientation: clamp spine vertical, cup upright.' Tall, thin vertical walls in SLA are prone to peel-force distortion.
issues.fix: Consider adding internal ribs or a slight outward draft (1–2°) to reduce peel forces, or re-orient the part so the cup wall prints at an angle (though this may conflict with the clamp spine orientation).
issues.problem: The cup wall is a 50 mm tall, 3 mm thick vertical cylinder printed upright. This orientation creates large peel forces on each layer and a tall unsupported span that may warp or delaminate.

issues.evidence: Drain cylinder at [57.5, 0, -64] to -59 mm (features:9) exits at z = -59 mm, which is 34 mm below the desk top at z = 0 (scene:desk). Liquid will fall onto the desk.
issues.fix: If desk protection is desired, add a small printed drip tray or route the drain away from the desk edge; otherwise leave as-is for drainage.
issues.problem: The 4 mm radius drain hole through the cup floor is open to the desk surface; any spilled liquid will drip onto the desk.

issues.evidence: Hole radius 3 mm (diameter 6 mm) matches M6 major diameter (features:6). Screw is retained by the lower jaw walls (scene:clamp_screw). No insert or thread feature is modelled.
issues.fix: If the screw will be adjusted frequently, consider tapping the hole post-print or adding a metal heat-set insert; otherwise the current geometry is functional.
issues.problem: The screw hole is a plain 3 mm radius cylinder through the lower jaw; an M6 screw (major diameter 6 mm) will cut its own threads in the resin, which is acceptable for light duty but may strip under repeated tightening.
